title: ContinuLoc: Continuous Pose Inference over Neural Fields for UAV Geo-Localization
claim: Coarse-to-fine inference over a continuous compatibility landscape concentrates pose hypotheses on the true location, steadily refining the match.
layout: 3 zones, left-to-right: map, zoomed inset, image grid; black zoom lines
description: The figure has three zones, read left to right. On the left is an aerial city map with a blue semi-transparent heat overlay and many small colored markers for pose candidates. A small black box marks a region. Black lines expand that region into a large center panel. The center panel shows a zoomed aerial view with white contour lines and a red-orange peak, which is the compatibility landscape. Blue circles, orange squares and green triangles mark candidates from Stage I, II and III. A yellow star marks the ground truth, and a legend sits in the top right. On the right, a grid of aerial photos shows the query and ground truth on top. Below them are the best views from Stage I, II and III, labeled with text. Later stages look closer to the ground truth.
caption: Illustration of ContinuLoc for UAV geo-localization. Left and center: visualization of the compatibility landscape, with pose candidates from the three inference stages. Right: the query image and reference views corresponding to the ground-truth pose and the highest-scoring pose at each stage.
abstract: Cross-view UAV geo-localization involves three design choices: how to represent the UAV observation, how to represent the geo-referenced map, and how to infer pose from their interaction. The dominant paradigm organizes the map as a discretized 2DoF candidate library, coupling map representation to pose inference and thus bounding spatial localization precision by candidate sampling resolution. We decouple map representation from pose inference by encoding the geo-referenced map as a continuously queryable semantic neural field, enabling localization to be formulated as explicit optimization over a continuous 4DoF pose space parameterized by 2D ground position, in-plane heading, and viewing scale. Pose hypotheses are evaluated on demand using global descriptors in a shared semantic feature space, bypassing the sampling bottleneck of retrieval. We learn 4DoF pose-sensitive visual representations under full 4DoF supervision provided by ContinuScenes, a multi-city benchmark with dense near-nadir UAV imagery and complete pose annotations. Inference proceeds hierarchically, progressing from broad pose-space coverage to adaptive concentration on high-compatibility regions. Experiments demonstrate substantial gains over representative localization paradigms under progressively stricter 4DoF accuracy criteria. Code is available at https://github.com/ZhouWeikun/ContinuLoc/
